title: Affine-curve cohomological dimension
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $C$ be a smooth affine curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves] (separated and of finite type over $k$, of dimension at most one, possibly empty or disconnected), and let $d\geq1$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. Let $\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}$ be the constant etale sheaf [def-sc-constant-sheaves], and use etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Then
$$H^q(C_{\Et},\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z})=0\qquad(q>1).$$
If $C$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], then also
$$H^0(C_{\Et},\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z})\cong\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z.$$
The latter identification is induced by constant sections. Connectedness is needed only for the degree-zero assertion.

proof.text: Put $F=\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}$. By [def-sc-constant-sheaves] this is the constant sheaf with the same value as the $\mathbf F_d$ appearing in the curve calculation. A section of the sheafification is locally represented by sections of the constant presheaf. Each representative lies in $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$ and is killed by $d$. Therefore the restriction of any section to such a representing cover is killed by $d>0$. Thus $F$ is torsion in the precise sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. By [def-sc-curves], $C$ is separated, finite type and has dimension at most one; no connectedness is inferred.

source.place: Proof, coefficient identification and hypotheses of the cited curve calculation

proof.text: First suppose $C$ is a connected curve in the dimension-one sense of [def-sc-curves]. Apply [thm-sc-affine-cohomology] with $n=d$: the field is algebraically closed, the curve is smooth, affine, nonempty and connected of dimension one, and $d$ is positive and prime to the characteristic. Its displayed $H^q(C_{\Et},\mathbf F_d)=0$ for $q>1$ gives the required higher-degree vanishing, and its displayed degree-zero isomorphism gives the degree-zero assertion in this case. No Kummer-sequence calculation or Picard assertion is needed beyond the statement of that existing theorem.

source.place: Proof, specialization of thm-sc-affine-cohomology to n=d

proof.text: The imported proof cannot apply the connected dimension-one theorem to an arbitrary curve. To retain all cases of the vanishing assertion, use the general affine bound [thm-sc-affine-torsion-cd]. For nonempty $C$, the algebraically closed field $k$ is separably closed, so [lem-sf-separably-closed-torsion-cd] gives $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(k)\leq0$. Apply the affine bound with $K=k$ and $c=0$, obtaining $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(C)\leq\dim C\leq1$. By [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], this means that $H^q(C,F)=0$ for every $q>1$, since $F$ is torsion by Step 1. This covers disconnected curves and zero-dimensional components without adding any geometric hypothesis. The connected dimension-one case remains the blueprint calculation in Step 2.

If $C$ is empty, every etale $C$-scheme is empty and the empty covering family is jointly surjective in [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The sheaf condition on this family forces the section group of every abelian sheaf at every object to be the zero group. Thus the global sections of each term of any resolution are zero; the complex defining [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] is zero and all its cohomology groups are zero. This completes the remaining case of higher-degree vanishing. The corrected degree-zero assertion does not apply to the empty curve.

source.place: Tag 03SC, theorem-vanishing-affine-curves (2), empty case from the empty-cover sheaf condition

proof.text: For the degree-zero identification on any nonempty connected $C$, compute cohomology by an ordinary injective resolution concentrated in nonnegative degrees. The sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves-grothendieck], hence has enough injectives by [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives]. Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] supplies such a resolution $F\to I^\bullet$. It is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so it computes the cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. The functor $\Gamma(C,-)$ is evaluation at the terminal object by [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor]; it is additive because addition of sheaf morphisms is sectionwise. For a morphism of abelian sheaves $a:G\to H$, the presheaf $U\mapsto\ker(a_U)$ is a sheaf: compatible sections glue uniquely in $G$, and their glued image is zero by uniqueness of gluing in $H$. Hence the kernel sheaf is computed sectionwise, and evaluation preserves kernels and is left exact. Part (2) of the degree-zero resolution lemma therefore gives the canonical isomorphism $H^0(C,F)\cong\Gamma(C,F)$. Concretely, this is the identification $\ker(\Gamma(I^0)\to\Gamma(I^1))=\Gamma(F)$, with no negative-degree boundaries.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected] to the nonempty connected scheme $C$ and the abelian group $E=\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z$. Its canonical constant-section map $E\to\Gamma(C,\underline E)$ is an isomorphism. Compose it with the inverse of the degree-zero comparison from Step 5 to obtain $\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z\xrightarrow{\sim}H^0(C,F)$. This proof also covers a connected zero-dimensional smooth affine curve; no dimension-one or Kummer hypothesis is used for this final identification.
